quizName: Hardest Questions in Arizona Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: Which color is best to wear so others can see you?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green when riding a motorcycle. Bright clothing helps others see you at any time of day.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective gear for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe riders wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles helps you:

options.text: React faster if another driver makes a mistake.
Stay in one spot in the lane and limit your movement.
Rely on other drivers to see hazards.
Go faster to keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: React faster if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of your normal checking routine.
Should be avoided because they distract you.
Should be avoided because other drivers can see you easily.
Are only needed in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal checking routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to know what is behind you. Regular mirror checks are an important part of safe riding.

questions.question: To check tire pressure correctly:

options.text: Look at the tire to judge its pressure.
Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare the tire height to another tire.

questions.explanation: Always use a tire gauge to check pressure before each ride. A low tire may look fine, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are typically made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: The best gear to wear while riding is:
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. Always wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, clothing:

options.text: Should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
Should not cover your arms or legs completely.
Does not need a jacket in warm weather.
Can protect you if you crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect you if you crash.
questions.explanation: Good clothing provides important protection in a crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, even when it is warm. Clothing should fit snugly but not restrict your movement.

questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Is usually too warm to wear while riding.
Should not be worn while riding.

questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved leather jacket when riding for protection. In warm weather, a leather jacket can help protect you and keep you cool. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to be comfortable in hot weather.

questions.question: Even if your turn is obvious, you:

options.text: Do not need to use a turn signal.
Should still use a turn signal.
Only need a turn signal if pedestrians are nearby.
Only need a turn signal at stop lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should still use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal when turning or changing lanes, even if you think it is obvious. Other vehicles nearby may not see you, even if you don't notice them.

questions.question: Your body can only get rid of alcohol through:
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted markings, and metal plates are all slippery. Dry pavement is the safest for motorcyclists.

questions.question: As a motorcycle rider, how can you help others see you?
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright colors, use your headlight all the time, and always use your turn signals.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should wear shoes with soles that are:
questions.explanation: Choose riding boots or shoes that are high and sturdy enough to protect your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: Where should you get the most information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is your best resource for information about your specific motorcycle. It covers how to operate it, maintain it, and its specifications.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Other drivers may go slowly while looking for a spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: A driver might pull out without looking. Car doors may open into your lane, or pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep going and hope you wake up.
Get off the road and rest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off the road and rest.
questions.explanation: Do not ride if you are tired. On long trips, stop and rest every two hours to avoid fatigue.

questions.question: Turn signals on a motorcycle are:

options.text: Not very important since motorcycles are small.
Very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Not needed if no other vehicles are close.
More complicated than those on a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are more vulnerable. Always use your turn signals when you turn or change lanes, even if no one is nearby.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Can reduce how serious a head injury is.
Makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can reduce how serious a head injury is.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet greatly reduces your risk of serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your side vision.

questions.question: What types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.

questions.question: The most important thing you can do to survive a crash is:

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is properly fastened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is properly fastened.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that is properly fastened is the most effective way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of an accident, you should:

options.text: Try to blend in and avoid being noticed by other drivers.
Only use turn signals at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
Ride very close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: To reduce the risk of a crash, make yourself visible to other drivers. Use turn signals, brake lights, and proper lane position to show your intentions. Keep a safe distance from other vehicles, look ahead 12 seconds, and be ready to act if danger appears.

questions.question: Use a turn signal:

options.text: When you plan to speed up.

questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal when you plan to turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Laced-up boots are best. If your boots have long laces, tie them up securely before riding.

questions.question: Riding with a passenger:

options.text: Does not change how the motorcycle handles.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to the motorcycle and affects how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Hide your intentions from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see and be seen better.
Keep you close to road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see and be seen better.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see other drivers and lets them see you. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing: sturdy pants and jackets that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: If you can't avoid a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: Proper motorcycle riding clothing should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Cover your arms, but leave your legs exposed.
Cover your legs, but leave your arms exposed.
Be whatever is most comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that completely cover your arms and legs for proper protection.

questions.question: Riding gloves should:

options.text: Not be worn because they make your hands too hot.
Be worn to grip the handlebars better.
Not be worn because they make it harder to use the controls.
Be worn only on cool days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn to grip the handlebars better.
questions.explanation: Wear leather gloves or gloves made of other sturdy materials. They give you a better grip on the handlebars and help protect your hands if you crash.
